evidence.quote: the Committee decided to maintain the target range for the federal funds rate at 4¼ to 4½ percent and to continue reducing the size of our balance sheet.
For the time being, we are well positioned to wait to learn more about the likely course of the economy before considering any adjustments to our policy stance.
everyone that I know is forecasting a meaningful increase in inflation in coming months from tariffs because someone has to pay for the tariffs.
So the labor market’s not crying out for a rate cut.
Our obligation is to keep longer-term inflation expectations well anchored and to prevent a one-time increase in the price level from becoming an ongoing inflation problem.
We know that the time will come; it come—could come quickly. It could not come quickly.

parsed.rationale: The Chair holds rates and emphasizes waiting to see tariff-driven inflation, with a solid labor market reducing urgency to cut, while the median dot still implies cuts this year and describes policy as only modestly restrictive. The net signal is a patient hold with a slight hawkish tilt from inflation concerns.
